Key date for Florida homebuyers

To qualify for the expanded homestead exemption under Amendment 3 beginning in 2027, a buyer must establish Florida permanent residency by December 31, 2026. Buyers who establish residency after that date receive the current exemption and become eligible for the expanded amount beginning in the fifth year of their homestead exemption.

General information only; not tax or legal advice. Please confirm details with your county Property Appraiser or a tax professional.

Amendment 3: Homestead Tax Exemption

Florida voters approved Amendment 3 in the November 2026 election, with about 62% of the vote (60% was required). For homeowners who live in the home as their primary residence, it raises the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, then adjusts it for inflation each year after 2028. School taxes keep their current $25,000 exemption.

The Save Our Homes 3% annual cap on homestead assessments is unchanged. For second homes, rentals and commercial property, the annual cap on assessment increases drops from 10% to 5% starting in 2027. The expanded exemption does not apply to investment properties or second homes.

Key date: Florida residency must be established by December 31, 2026. Buyers who establish residency after that date receive the current exemption ($25,000 for school taxes and up to $50,000 for non-school taxes), and the expanded amount beginning in the fifth year of their exemption.

This is general information only and is not tax or legal advice. Please confirm details with a tax professional or your county Property Appraiser. Sources: Florida Dept. of Revenue, PTO 26-21 · HJR 1-F · Florida Policy Institute · FOX 13
